findings.problem: The 'one web component' rule for vendor eligibility is bypassed. The shared vendors/Eligibility component renders not-eligible as a Signal with tone "danger" and reasons as "first reason and N more". The PO-create path re-implements it inline as `Signal tone="warning"` with `vendor.reasons.join("; ")`, so the same state ships with two tones (amber here, red elsewhere) and two reason formats. vendors/editor/InvitedVendorsCard.tsx:27 does the same a third way: plain secondary text with no icon or tone at all for an invited (not-eligible) vendor, while its own Picker path (line 87) uses the shared component. Eligibility is decided by the server in all three, so the drift is display-only, but it defeats the single-component story's purpose and muddies the status vocabulary E11-S09 aligns.
findings.fix: Give the shared Eligibility component a variant that covers the invited/inline row and the award-lines header, and route both AwardedLines.tsx and InvitedVendorsCard.tsx through it so tone and reason phrasing are single-sourced.

findings.problem: Money is rendered two ways across the milestone: the shared ui/Money component applies the MASTER money rule (parenthesised negatives, a sign icon, and a `data-negative` colour via tokens), but BidSheet renders its line totals and totals inline as `formatMoney(x, currency, navigator.language) + ' ' + currency` (lines 196, 237, 247, 258) with no `<Money>` import, no sign icon and no negative colour, and the currency code appended outside the `.project-currency` span. It also passes `navigator.language` where the shared component uses the en-US default plus `separators()`, so grouping can diverge from the rest of the app. Bid line amounts are non-negative today, so this is latent rather than an active failure.
findings.fix: Route the bid sheet's monetary cells through the shared `<Money>` component (or a single formatting helper that also applies sign/colour), and drop the ad-hoc `navigator.language` locale in favour of the app's shared formatter.
